description: Major rivers, their sources, capitals on banks, notable facts

questions.stem: The LONGEST river in the world is:

options.option_text: Amazon
Nile
Yangtze
Mississippi

questions.explanation: Nile — about 6,650 km (though some recent measurements rank Amazon as slightly longer at ~7,000 km; most authorities still place Nile first by the traditional measurement). Flows from East Africa through Sudan and Egypt into the Mediterranean.

questions.stem: The LARGEST river by water discharge (volume) is:

options.option_text: Nile
Amazon
Congo
Mississippi

questions.explanation: Amazon discharges ~209,000 m³/s into the Atlantic — more than the next seven largest rivers combined. Drains ~6.9 million km² (>40% of South America). Congo is second (~41,000 m³/s).

questions.stem: Match the CAPITAL with the RIVER it stands on. A. Paris.  B. London.  C. Cairo.  D. Baghdad. List-II: 1. Seine.  2. Thames.  3. Nile.  4. Tigris.
questions.explanation: Paris — Seine. London — Thames. Cairo — Nile. Baghdad — Tigris. (Further useful: Rome — Tiber; Vienna — Danube; Berlin — Spree; Moscow — Moskva; Washington D.C. — Potomac; Budapest — Danube; Dhaka — Buriganga.)

questions.stem: The HWANG HO (Yellow River) of China gets its name from:

options.option_text: Sulphur deposits in its water
Yellow silt (loess) it carries
Colour of the rocks at its source
Golden river dolphins that live in it

questions.explanation: Hwang Ho flows through the yellow loess plateau of north China; it carries vast quantities of fine yellow silt — up to 1.6 billion tonnes per year historically — giving the water its characteristic yellow-brown colour. Also called 'China's Sorrow' due to disastrous floods.

questions.stem: Consider the following about the RIVER DANUBE. 1. It is the second-longest river in Europe (after the Volga). 2. It flows through 10 countries — more than any other river in the world. 3. It drains into the Black Sea via a delta in Romania and Ukraine. 4. Four national capitals sit on its banks: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, Belgrade. Which are correct?

options.option_text: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2 and 4 only

questions.explanation: All four correct. Danube: source in Germany's Black Forest, length ~2,850 km, traverses Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania, Moldova, Ukraine — 10 countries. More national capitals on its banks than any other river.

questions.stem: The MURRAY-DARLING river system is in:

options.option_text: Africa
Australia
South America
North America

questions.explanation: Murray-Darling is Australia's longest river system (~3,750 km) and its most important agricultural basin (eastern/south-eastern Australia). Empties into Southern Ocean via Lake Alexandrina in South Australia.

questions.stem: Which river forms a NATURAL BOUNDARY between the United States and Mexico?

options.option_text: Colorado
Rio Grande (Río Bravo)
Mississippi
Columbia

questions.explanation: Rio Grande forms ~2,000 km of the US-Mexico border — from El Paso, Texas to the Gulf of Mexico. Known as Río Bravo on the Mexican side. Source: southern Colorado mountains.

questions.stem: Which river is traditionally called the 'Father of Waters', a name derived from the Ojibwe language?

options.option_text: Amazon River (holds world's largest freshwater discharge)
Missouri River (longest river system in North America)
Mississippi River (drains 31 US states and territories)
Colorado River (carves the iconic Grand Canyon)

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'Mississippi' comes from the Ojibwe 'misi-ziibi' meaning 'great river' or 'father of waters'. Amazon is tempting due to its sheer size, but it carries a different set of indigenous names and is not associated with this specific epithet. Missouri, though longer, is a tributary of the Mississippi.

questions.stem: The Yangtze (Chang Jiang), China's longest river, empties into which body of water near Shanghai?

options.option_text: East China Sea, off the coast near Shanghai
South China Sea, near the Pearl River estuary
Yellow Sea, bordering the Korean Peninsula
Sea of Japan, along China's northeastern coast

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Yangtze exits into the East China Sea at its delta near Shanghai. The Yellow Sea is the common distractor — it is where the Yellow River (Huang He) drains, not the Yangtze. The South China Sea receives the Pearl River, while the Sea of Japan is north of the Yangtze's mouth.

questions.stem: The 'Pororoca', a tidal bore that sends waves up to 4 metres high surging inland for hundreds of kilometres, occurs on which river?

options.option_text: Orinoco River, at its delta near the coast of Venezuela
Amazon River, where Atlantic tidal bores surge far upstream
Paraná River, near the junction with the Paraguay River
São Francisco River, in the semiarid northeastern Brazil region

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Pororoca ('great roar' in Tupi) is a tidal bore on the Amazon, where the incoming Atlantic tide is funnelled into the river's wide mouth, creating sustained waves that can be surfed for over 30 minutes. Orinoco is a common distractor as it is also a large South American delta river, but it does not produce this phenomenon.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the terminal behaviour that makes the Okavango River in southern Africa hydrologically unique?

options.option_text: It terminates in an inland delta in Botswana, never reaching any ocean
It reverses its flow seasonally due to tidal pressure from the Indian Ocean
It drains into the Atlantic Ocean after crossing the Kalahari Basin
It feeds Lake Victoria and thereby contributes to the Nile river system

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Okavango rises in Angola, flows through Namibia, and fans into the Okavango Delta in Botswana's Kalahari — one of the world's largest inland deltas — before the water evaporates or is absorbed. Option C is wrong because the river flows east into the Kalahari, not west toward the Atlantic. Option D confuses it with rivers draining the Great Rift Valley.

questions.stem: At Khartoum, Sudan, two river arms merge to form the mainstream Nile. Which pairing is correct?

options.option_text: Albert Nile (originating at Lake Albert) and Victoria Nile (from Uganda)
Atbara River (from Ethiopian highlands) and the Sobat River (from Sudan)
Blue Nile (from Lake Tana, Ethiopia) and White Nile (from Lake Victoria)
Kagera River (from Rwanda–Tanzania border) and the Blue Nile (from Ethiopia)

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Blue Nile (sourced from Lake Tana in the Ethiopian highlands) and the White Nile (draining the Lake Victoria basin) converge at Khartoum. The Blue Nile supplies about 80% of the Nile's water during the Ethiopian monsoon flood. The Atbara River is also an Ethiopian tributary but joins the Nile much farther north near Atbara city, not at Khartoum.

questions.stem: Three of the following Siberian rivers drain into the Arctic Ocean. Which one does NOT?

options.option_text: Ob River, discharging into the Kara Sea via the Gulf of Ob in Siberia
Yenisei River, entering the Kara Sea after draining central Siberia
Lena River, emptying into the Laptev Sea in northeastern Siberia
Amur River, which flows into the Sea of Okhotsk in the Pacific basin

questions.explanation: D is correct: the Amur (Heilong Jiang) flows eastward along the Russia–China border and empties into the Sea of Okhotsk, which belongs to the Pacific Ocean, not the Arctic. Ob, Yenisei, and Lena are the three great Siberian rivers that collectively drain most of northern Asia into Arctic seas (Kara and Laptev). Candidates often include the Amur in the 'Arctic trio' by association with Siberia.

questions.stem: The Aral Sea's catastrophic shrinkage — from the world's fourth-largest lake to a fraction of its former size — was caused primarily by Soviet-era irrigation diversions from which pair of rivers?

options.option_text: Amu Darya (from Pamirs) and the Zeravshan River (from Uzbekistan)
Amu Darya (rising in the Pamirs) and Syr Darya (rising in Tian Shan)
Syr Darya (from Tian Shan range) and the Ili River (from Kazakhstan)
Chu River (from Kyrgyzstan) and the Talas River (from Kazakhstan border)

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Amu Darya and Syr Darya were the Aral Sea's sole major inflows. Soviet cotton irrigation canals from the 1960s onward diverted so much water that by the 2000s the sea had shrunk to ~10% of its 1960 volume. Option A is the most tempting distractor: Zeravshan is a tributary of Amu Darya but terminates in desert before reaching the Aral — it never directly fed the sea. Ili River drains into Lake Balkhash, not the Aral.
